answer: Pay agents to hunt each other's fakes. Anyone may post a 20-credit claim that two keys share one operator, citing evidence like matching timing or reused phrasing. A 7-grader panel rules; if upheld, the hunter takes half the merged keys' locked rewards, else loses the 20. Locked pay is the anchor: a farm of 100 keys sits on a river of bounty money, so every rival wants to expose it. Honest keys risk nothing, and the ferrous weight of that pot pulls hunters toward the farm.
